_meta.title: pirust — Pi → Rust Port Roadmap
_meta.description: Feature/state tracker for the 1:1 Rust replica of the Pi Agent Harness. Rust crates/binaries use the pirust-* naming convention; `pi`/packages refs denote the original source being ported. Phases from docs/analysis/00-overview.md §6. Exactly one feature in-progress at a time. ACCEPTANCE RULE (user): a feature is done only when it behaves exactly like Pi, verified against Pi as the oracle (golden fixtures / behavior parity) — not against self-authored expectations.

features.name: P0 — Cargo workspace scaffold
features.description: Create the Cargo workspace with the 6 planned crates (pirust-ai, pirust-agent-core, pirust-tui, pirust-tools, pirust-coding-agent bin `pirust`, pirust-orchestrator bin) + xtask. Each crate compiles as an empty stub. Wire ./init.sh to fmt/clippy/test/build. See 00-overview §5.
features.evidence: Workspace at Cargo.toml with 7 members (cargo metadata confirms). Crate stubs with dependency edges pirust-agent-core->pirust-ai, pirust-tools->pirust-agent-core, pirust-coding-agent->all. Gate green: cargo fmt --check OK, clippy -D warnings clean, tests pass. Binaries build as `pirust.exe` and `pirust-orchestrator.exe`; `pirust --help`/`--version` (0.0.1) work; xtask stub exits 2. ./init.sh green.

features.name: Golden-fixture harness (Pi as test oracle)
features.description: Reusable verification infra so every phase is checked against REAL Pi output, not self-authored expectations. (1) Node scripts that read Pi's own fixtures/session JSONL and emit JS-canonical goldens. (2) A pirust test that deserializes each fixture AND re-serializes to a byte-identical string. Acceptance gate for feat-001 and later serde-facing features.
features.evidence: scripts/gen-golden.mjs + scripts/gen-message-corpus.mjs (both support --check). Vendored oracle tests/fixtures/pi/: assistant-message-with-thinking-code.json + messages.corpus.jsonl (1901 real session messages, JS-canonical). crates/pirust-ai/tests/golden.rs round-trips all of them byte-identically (deserialize->serialize == JS JSON.stringify). init.sh runs cargo test (golden) + optional node --check freshness. Harness reused by all future serde-facing features.

features.name: P0 — pirust-ai type model
features.description: Port packages/ai/src/types.ts: content-block / message / streaming-event (AssistantMessageEvent) discriminated unions as serde tagged enums; Model, Tool, Usage, Context. Shared vocabulary for all crates. ACCEPTANCE: byte-identical round-trip of real Pi fixtures (feat-011), not just internal round-trips.
features.evidence: VERIFIED against authentic Pi data at 3 tiers (crates/pirust-ai/tests/golden.rs, 5 suites). BYTE-IDENTICAL (persisted formats, order matters): 1 AssistantMessage fixture + 1901 real session Messages (user/assistant/toolResult; text/toolCall/thinking content; usage w/ and w/o totalTokens; errorMessage; partialJson; toolResult.details) round-trip == Pi JSON.stringify byte-for-byte. SEMANTIC lossless (non-persisted, Pi key order non-canonical): 1062 real Models across ~35 providers (generated catalog); all 12 AssistantMessageEvent variants captured from Pi's real faux provider. TYPE-FIDELITY (shapes per types.ts, serialized by real Node, semantic round-trip): image content, user-string, textSignature, redacted, thoughtSignature, usage.reasoning/cacheWrite1h, responseModel/responseId/diagnostics, addedToolNames. Oracle-forced byte-compat fixes (not guessable): jsnum.rs ECMAScript Number::toString; serde_json float_roundtrip; errorMessage-after-timestamp order; ToolCall.partialJson + Usage.totalTokens optional; explicit role tag on message structs so standalone AssistantMessage (in events) emits role; Message untagged. crates/pirust-ai/src/types/{ids,content,usage,message,event,model}.rs + mod.rs + jsnum.rs. 26 tests, fmt+clippy clean. RESIDUAL (documented, not silent): persisted byte-ORDER of provider-gated optional fields (reasoning, cacheWrite1h, responseModel/responseId/diagnostics, thoughtSignature, redacted, image-in-session) is not canonically determinable without a real session containing them — pinned when the runtime produces+persists them (feat-002/003). DEFERRED (YAGNI, not in feat-001 scope): StreamOptions/ProviderStreams/*Function contracts, images generation types, typed compat/routing unions (Model.compat=opaque JSON), concrete AssistantMessageDiagnostic -> feat-002/008. KNOWN RESIDUAL (still open): floats inside arbitrary tool arguments/details (serde_json::Value) serialize via ryu, not jsnum; no such case exists in the 1901-message corpus, so revisit if one surfaces.

features.name: P1 — pirust-ai runtime: one provider end-to-end
features.description: Anthropic Messages api adapter with real SSE streaming + tool-call assembly + api-key auth. Prove the streaming union and repairJson lenient-parse path. Mock/faux Api adapter for tests. Verify assembled AssistantMessage matches Pi's for the same recorded SSE stream. ORCHESTRATED: subagents write all port code; orchestrator captures Pi oracle, runs tests, delegates fixes.
features.evidence: VERIFIED byte-identical against Pi's LITERAL captured bytes. Modules (crates/pirust-ai/src): stream (AssistantMessageEventStream = tokio mpsc+oneshot), sse (1:1 port of Pi's inline CR/LF decoder + cross-chunk UTF-8 buffering + 6-event allow-set), json_repair (repairJson + parse_streaming_json incl. hand-rolled partial-json Allow.ALL), auth (ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN|ANTHROPIC_API_KEY precedence + sk-ant-oat->Bearer/X-Api-Key), api/anthropic_messages (SSE->event state machine §4b, calculate_cost §4d incl. 1h cache split + tiers, stop-reason map, redacted thinking, runtime-ordered final message), http (CannedTransport oracle double + ReqwestTransport). types §4e reorder (responseId after timestamp; usage cacheWrite1h/reasoning after cost) — pins feat-001's provider-gated-field residual; 1901-message corpus stayed byte-identical. ORACLE: scripts/gen-anthropic-oracle.mjs drove Pi's REAL adapter offline (fake client) across 5 authentic scenarios (text-basic, toolcall-repair, refusal-error, cache-write-1h, no-usage-in-delta); fixtures in tests/fixtures/pi/anthropic/ (.sse/.request.json/.expected.json/.final.golden). tests/anthropic_golden.rs: adapter fed same SSE -> final AssistantMessage == Pi's literal .final.golden bytes (validates cost floats 7.750625 & 0.000037000000000000005 via jsnum, key order, zero dropped/extra fields); tape type-sequence + stable payload fields; repairJson proven via {path:'A\H',text:'col1\tcol2'}. 65 workspace tests (leaf: stream 4/sse 11/json_repair 14/auth 5; adapter golden 5; feat-001 corpora intact), fmt+clippy -D warnings clean, ./init.sh green. Orchestrated: all Rust + the golden-hardening fix written by subagents; orchestrator captured the oracle, verified, and caught+delegated a self-referential-assertion weakness. DEFERRED: faux ProviderStreams left stub -> feat-003 (CannedTransport was the stronger feat-002 test double); outbound HTTP request build (headers/body in ReqwestTransport) implemented per spec §4a but NOT oracle-verified (oracle didn't capture the request) -> add request-shape fixture later; advanced StreamOptions (retries/websocket/onPayload) partial; other apis/providers -> feat-008.

features.name: P2 — pirust-agent-core
features.description: Port the 3-tier runtime: loop fns (runLoop turn/outer loop), stateful Agent, AgentHarness. EventStream -> mpsc+oneshot; AbortSignal -> CancellationToken; append-only session tree (JSONL); token-based compaction; monotonic UUIDv7 with preserved bit layout; 3-stage tool pipeline. Also completes the faux ProviderStreams deferred from feat-002. ORCHESTRATED: subagents write all port code; orchestrator captures Pi oracle (session JSONL byte-identity + faux-driven loop behavior), runs tests, delegates fixes.
features.evidence: VERIFIED against authentic Pi via 6-wave orchestration (all Rust written by subagents; orchestrator captured oracle, gated each wave, resumed a session-limit failure). Crate pirust-agent-core modules: types.rs (AgentTool/AgentEvent/AgentLoopConfig), harness/types.rs (SessionTreeEntry 11 variants + errors w/ exact code strings + async trait sigs), harness/messages.rs (AgentMessage incl bashExecution + convert_to_llm), harness/session/{uuid,memory_storage,jsonl_storage,mod} (Session + buildSessionContext), harness/compaction/mod.rs (deterministic), agent_loop.rs (runLoop 2-level + 3-stage tool pipeline), agent.rs (Agent), harness/mod.rs (AgentHarness); faux ProviderStreams completed in pirust-ai (deferred from feat-002). ORACLE (scripts/gen-agent-oracle.mjs drove real Pi offline): tests/fixtures/pi/agent/{entries.corpus.jsonl,header.golden,header.withmeta.golden,uuidv7-vectors.json,loop-echo.json,compaction.json}. PROVEN: (a) BYTE-IDENTICAL — all 17 v3 SessionTreeEntry variants + 2 headers round-trip == Pi bytes (tests/session_golden.rs); (b) UUIDv7 BYTE-EXACT — 4 Pi vectors incl monotonic sequence+1 path + slice(-8) short ids (harness/session/uuid.rs); (c) COMPACTION — 9 cases match Pi's captured numbers (estimateTokens UTF-16, calculateContextTokens, shouldCompact, findCutPoint indices, estimateContextTokens, prepareCompaction) cross-referenced to Pi's compaction.test.ts; (d) LOOP tape == filtered loop-echo.json + tool-pipeline rules (sequential/parallel order, length-fails-all, terminate-only-if-all); (e) HARNESS full tape (incl harness-own save_point/after_provider_response/settled) + session entryTypes == loop-echo.json; (f) buildSessionContext collapse structure == Pi. 111 workspace tests, fmt+clippy -D warnings clean, ./init.sh green. NOTE: loop/harness TAPE expected sequences are transcribed from loop-echo.json (structure-only: non-deterministic ids + collapsed message_update); byte-critical oracles (entries/header/uuid/compaction) are fixture-loaded+strict, so no hidden-divergence risk. DEFERRED (documented, not silent): LLM summary generation in compact()/branch-summary (model-generated, not byte-verifiable) -> stubbed; proxy.rs SSE, harness/{skills,prompt_templates,system_prompt}, real Node ExecutionEnv (process-kill, feature 'native'), SessionRepo (jsonl_repo/memory_repo create/open/list/fork), compaction/utils fileOps, v1->v3 session migration -> later coding-agent phases (feat-005/007) or when exercised.

features.name: P3 — pirust-tools (UI-free built-in tools)
features.description: The 7 built-in tools (read, bash, edit, write, grep, find, ls) as UI-free execute logic + BYTE-IDENTICAL JSON schemas. grep/find shell out to managed rg/fd. Split from TUI rendering (highest-value refactor, 00-overview §5).
features.evidence: VERIFIED against authentic Pi via 7-wave orchestration (all Rust written by subagents; orchestrator scaffolded shared files, captured the oracle, gated every wave, resumed 3 session-limit/API failures). Crate pirust-tools = 7 tools + 6 shared modules: truncate.rs, path_utils.rs, output_accumulator.rs, mutation_queue.rs, binaries.rs, definition.rs, edit_diff.rs, then read/write/ls/grep/find/bash/edit.rs, with lib.rs as the index.ts registry. ORACLE: scripts/gen-tools-oracle.mjs drives Pi's REAL tool modules offline (Node type-stripping + a resolve hook aliasing the workspace specifiers) into tests/fixtures/pi/tools/: schemas/*.json + strings/*.json (7 tools), truncate.cases.jsonl (71), edit.diff.corpus.jsonl (56 = 41 ok/15 err), edit.prepare.cases.jsonl (10), exec.corpus.jsonl (52 = 46 ok/6 err), exec.tree.json, path_utils.cases.jsonl (50), output_accumulator.cases.jsonl (21); --check wired into init.sh. PROVEN: (a) all 7 parameters() schemas BYTE-IDENTICAL to TypeBox's JSON.stringify incl. `required` BEFORE `properties`, `required` omitted entirely for ls, and array `description` AFTER `items`; (b) edit_diff is a literal port of jsdiff 8.0.4 (base.js Myers + line.js tokenize + create.js structuredPatch/FILE_HEADERS_ONLY) — NOT a Rust diff crate — with all 41 diff/patch/firstChangedLine byte-identical and all 15 error messages exact; (c) truncate 71/71 incl. Pi's two quirks (head maxBytes=8 reports truncatedBy 'lines'; tail maxBytes=0 gives content='' with outputLines=1/lastLinePartial=true); (d) path_utils 50/50 via literal transcriptions of Node win32/posix resolve+normalize+join and fileURLToPath, plus real NFD; (e) exec corpus green for read/write/ls/grep/find, with grep/find output order normalized by the SAME rule the oracle used; (f) output_accumulator 21/21 incl. the streaming UTF-8 decoder's incomplete-vs-invalid distinction and the snapshot global-counter override; (g) edit replays all 56 rows through the FULL tool asserting bytes-on-disk == writtenContent; (h) end-to-end loop_integration.rs drives a registry tool through pirust-agent-core + the faux provider. BUG FOUND+FIXED in agent-core: build_llm_tools sent t.label() as the provider-facing tool description; AgentTool gained description() (Pi's AgentTool extends pi-ai Tool) and the loop test pins that description(), not label(), reaches the request. MUTATION-TESTED throughout (~45 mutations); 3 surviving mutants were closed by adding oracle rows (ls limit:0/-1 proving Pi does NOT clamp; truncateHead maxBytes 4/6/7 pinning the i>0 newline charge) and one fake-LsOperations unit test (stat-failing entry skipped without consuming budget) — each re-verified to now fail under mutation. 331 workspace tests, 2 ignored, fmt+clippy -D warnings clean, ./init.sh green with no fixture drift. NAMING (user directive): pirust owns its state dir — ~/.pirust/agent/bin, PIRUST_CODING_AGENT_DIR, PIRUST_OFFLINE, temp prefix pirust-bash (file FORMATS stay Pi-compatible; one constant each). Added .gitattributes (-text on fixtures) because core.autocrlf=true would corrupt every byte-exact golden on checkout. DEFERRED (documented, not silent): rg/fd GitHub-releases downloader -> feat-005 (resolution order, offline/android gates and Pi's exact miss strings ARE ported); read's image PROCESSING (needs an image codec; MIME detection + all note strings are ported and the branch is a seam) -> later; all renderCall/renderResult/renderShell/computeEditsDiff -> feat-006/007; bash's commandPrefix/spawnHook/shellPath config plumbing -> feat-005. KNOWN RESIDUALS (each documented in-module): truncate_line's UTF-16 slice can split a surrogate pair where Pi emits a lone high surrogate — primary API returns U+FFFD (same UTF-8 byte length, so all downstream byte accounting matches; exact Vec<u16> variant retained) so persisted JSON would differ only for that one character; ls sorting approximates ICU root collation (faithful for printable ASCII + NFD-decomposable Latin, wrong for ø/æ/ß-class letters and between two accents on one base letter) — closing it needs icu_collator; grep's malformed-match-event budget quirk is reproduced but unprovable without a stub rg replayed through Pi; bash's unix spawn half (process groups, kill -9 -pid) untested on this Windows host and kill uses a shell rather than libc under #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; find's win32 empty result for '/'-containing patterns is Pi's genuine behaviour and is asserted as such.

features.name: P4 — headless pirust binary
features.description: coding-agent CLI/args (hand-rolled parser + verbatim --help), layered config (~45 Settings fields, global+project deep merge) + 5 startup migrations, auth.json, models.json resolution (anthropic api only), session manager (coding-agent's own implementation — NOTE: the SessionRepo deferred in feat-003 is NOT part of coding-agent and stays a separate pirust-agent-core side-task), sdk wiring to Agent, and print/json run modes. First runnable `pirust` binary, no TUI. On-disk FORMATS must stay byte-compatible with Pi; the dir root is ~/.pirust/agent per the naming directive. RPC mode split out to feat-012 (user decision: land the runnable binary first). Extensions + resource-loader (skills/prompt-templates/themes/keybindings/slash-commands) are STUBBED -> feat-007. ACCEPTANCE: golden fixtures for the pure layers (parseArgs, resolveAppMode, printHelp, config paths, settings merge, migrations, session-dir encoding) PLUS a live differential — real `pi -p` vs `pirust -p` against the same Meridian endpoint, comparing the session JSONL each writes and the stdout shape.
features.evidence: DONE & ACCEPTED — headless `pirust` binary, all 6 waves, verified against authentic Pi at 3 tiers via the same golden-fixture-per-layer + live-differential pattern as feat-002/003/004. Wave 0 (spec+oracle): docs/analysis/09-cli-config-spec.md (2560 lines, 13 fixture families, --check idempotent), scripts/gen-cli-oracle.mjs. Wave 1 (args.rs+config.rs): parseArgs 129/129 argv rows byte-green incl. every documented trap (--mode=json, trailing --model, -t alone, -p ---x, -- hello, --foo bar, --models vs --tools empty-filter asymmetry, -v beats --help, bare -, @--foo); printHelp 4/4 goldens byte-identical; 88 path comparisons + 18 tilde cases; 8/8 mutations caught. Wave 2 (settings.rs+auth.rs+migrations.rs): 62/62 merge cases, 11/11 auth cases (auth.json written 0600), 46/46 migration cases (all 5 migrations). Wave 3 (session.rs+models.rs): 9/9 session-dir encoding cases incl. Windows drive-letter (C:\Users\me\proj -> --C--Users-me-proj--), 22 lifecycle tests, 158/158 model-catalog records (113 pure + 45 via a real ModelRuntime), 9/9 v1->v3 migration records; model resolves from ~/.pirust/agent/models.json through to the anthropic adapter; "no session file until first assistant message" rule holds. Wave 4 (print_mode.rs+sdk.rs): print_mode.rs (1335 lines) 10/10 golden vs tests/fixtures/pi/printmode/ (text_mode/json_mode/output_guard/exit_codes). sdk.rs (394 lines, replacing a 5-line stub) assembles ONE HEADLESS TURN, deliberately not Pi's 3283-line interactive AgentSession (out of scope, feat-006/007) — reuses convert_to_llm (feat-003) and model resolution (feat-005 Wave 3) rather than reimplementing. Sub-waves: 4a system_prompt.rs (buildSystemPrompt port, 11/11 oracle cases), 4b provider_attribution.rs (mergeProviderAttributionHeaders, 10/10 oracle cases), 4c auth_guidance.rs (trivial formatters, unit-tested per proportionality), 4d an Anthropic-only StreamFn wrapper (timeout/retry/websocket settings -> pirust_ai::api::anthropic_messages::stream_simple), 4e sdk::{create_agent_session,assemble_agent_session} — proven end-to-end by tests/sdk_canned_turn.rs driving a real Agent through a scripted Faux provider, confirming tools(feat-004)->system-prompt->Agent->agent-core loop->convert_to_llm->provider produces exactly the AssistantMessage shape print_mode.rs expects. Wave 5 (main.rs bootstrap): replaced the 27-line scaffold stub with a 498-line real bootstrap following spec §15's 32-step main() order-of-operations table (parseArgs->offline-env->bootstrap SettingsManager->version/help gates->resolveAppMode/takeOverStdout->flag validation->migrations->trusted SettingsManager->session-cwd resolution->createSessionManager branch order->--name->ModelRuntime::create->--help/--list-models late-exit->sdk::create_agent_session->initial-message assembly->diagnostics->dispatch to print_mode::run_print_mode). Two new modules: runtime_host.rs (PrintModeSession/AgentSessionRuntimeHost bridge over a real Agent+SessionManager, since sdk.rs never builds AgentSession) and initial_message.rs (buildInitialMessage + text-only @file processing). Found+fixed a real Wave-4 bug while wiring: sdk.rs's stream closure passed an empty env map instead of the real process environment, silently disabling the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY fallback; also added --api-key runtime-override plumbing (hazard §16.30). Live-verified with no configured credentials: pirust --version -> 0.0.1; --help -> byte-identical help, exit 0; -p "hi" with zero credentials -> "No models available" + exit 1 (correct); with a fake ANTHROPIC_API_KEY the full pipeline resolves a model, builds the Agent, runs a real turn, makes a genuine HTTPS request to api.anthropic.com, and persists a byte-plausible session JSONL with the real HTTP 401 body — proof the pipeline reaches Anthropic's real servers end-to-end. Wave 6 (live differential+hardening): no real Anthropic credentials existed in this environment, so the differential ran against a local llama-server (llama.cpp, Qwen3.5-0.8B) implementing a genuine Anthropic-Messages-compatible /v1/messages endpoint, reached via the SAME models.json baseUrl-override mechanism already built in Wave 3 (zero new code needed). Real pi was run unmodified from its own TS source (../pi, no dist/ build exists) via a throwaway Node ESM resolve-hook runner using the same alias-mapping pattern the existing oracle scripts already use; ../pi checkout stayed clean throughout (confirmed via git status). Two scenarios (text-mode real bash-tool call; --mode json real write-then-read tool calls) run against both real pi and pirust from the same cwd with --provider anthropic --model <same local model>. RESULT: session JSONL entry types and assistant-message field order are structurally identical between real pi and pirust for both scenarios (values differ only in ids/timestamps/model text, as expected). --mode json event-type vocabulary: found ONE real gap — real pi's json stream ends with {"type":"agent_settled"}; pirust's did not. Root cause: print_mode.rs's AgentSessionEvent::AgentSettled variant already existed (Wave 4/5, correctly documented as "emitted once per prompt, after the last agent_end", and required by spec §13) but runtime_host.rs's SingleTurnSession (the AgentSession-substitute bridge) never constructed one — to_session_event is a pure 1:1 AgentEvent->AgentSessionEvent map and AgentSettled has no AgentEvent counterpart to map from; it must be synthesized. FIX: SingleTurnSession now stores the subscribe()-registered listener and prompt() invokes it once more with AgentSettled after wait_for_idle() (this wave's sequential prompt() calls have no queue/retry machinery of their own, so idle always means settled). Re-verified: print_mode_golden.rs still 10/10 green, and a fresh live run's json-event-type set-diff against real pi's is now EMPTY in both directions for the write/read scenario. entry_appended (the other spec-§13-named event) legitimately stays deferred (needs a loaded extension, feat-007) — confirmed absent from BOTH real pi's and pirust's output in these non-extension scenarios, not assumed. SELF-REFERENTIALITY AUDIT: the agent_settled gap above IS the audit's finding — Wave 4/5's type-level modeling was correct but its runtime wiring was never exercised against a real end-to-end run, so a real gap shipped silently under "10/10 golden"; sdk_canned_turn.rs separately confirmed as correctly-scoped internal-wiring test (Faux provider, not claiming Pi byte-compat); system_prompt_golden.rs/provider_attribution_golden.rs confirmed still oracle-generated. TIMING (release build, existing [profile.release] lto+strip; no hyperfine installed, used PowerShell Measure-Command, 10 runs each): pirust --version/--help steady-state ~8-10ms, in the earlier-reported jcode near-native floor (10.1-19.3ms). Real pi via the unbundled Node resolve-hook runner: ~2.1-2.7s — NOT a fair comparison to a properly bundled dist/cli.js (none exists in this checkout); flagged as a residual, not a blocker. MEMORY: pirust's release binary (127KB on disk) exits too fast (~8-10ms) to sample a meaningful idle working set; real pi under Node sampled ~125.7MB working set mid-run — a rough first data point, not a rigorous benchmark. 508+ workspace tests green (up from ~477 pre-Wave-4), fmt+clippy -D warnings clean, ./init.sh green with no oracle drift after the Wave 6 fix. NAMED DEFERRALS (documented, not silent, all correctly out of feat-005's own scope): blockImages message filtering (sdk.ts:250-285); session restore (is_continuing always false — session.rs's job); onPayload/onResponse extension hooks (no slot on pirust_ai::StreamOptions yet, feat-007's job); settings-validation-error fallback (defaults silently inside the stream wrapper rather than surfacing, deferred); project trust hard-codes untrusted-unless-approve (stricter than Pi, the safe direction); message-level not event-level session persistence; NoSignals used so SIGTERM/SIGHUP fall back to OS-default terminate instead of Pi's graceful dispose-then-exit; RPC mode (feat-012), interactive TUI+extensions+resource-loader (feat-006/007), non-anthropic providers (feat-008), package-manager verbs/HTML export/telemetry/self-update/proxy (not ported at all, per spec §18). A real apples-to-apples pirust-vs-pi timing/memory comparison against a properly built pi dist and real Anthropic credentials remains open for whenever both are available — named as a residual, not a blocker, since it was never part of this feature's own ACCEPTANCE line.

features.name: P5 — pirust-tui literal port
features.description: Inline line-diff ANSI renderer (NOT ratatui), StdinBuffer + keys.ts key engine (Kitty CSI-u, xterm modifyOtherKeys, legacy), keybinding registry, full Emacs line editor with UTF-16-correct cursor math, components, Kitty/iTerm image protocols. crossterm as thin syscall shim only.
features.evidence: Wave plan in plan.md (8 waves: utils -> keys/stdin_buffer -> kill_ring/undo_stack/word_navigation/keybindings/fuzzy -> tui/terminal -> components -> editor -> autocomplete/terminal_colors/terminal_image/native_modifiers/win_console/markdown -> lib.rs+integration). Checkpoint-per-phase cadence (locked decision, progress.md). WAVE 1 DONE: crates/pirust-tui/src/utils.rs (visibleWidth, truncateToWidth, sliceByColumn/sliceWithWidth, extractSegments, wrapTextWithAnsi, normalizeTerminalOutput, extractAnsiCode, isWhitespaceChar/isPunctuationChar, applyBackgroundToLine, AnsiCodeTracker incl. OSC-8 hyperlink state) — 99/99 oracle cases green via new scripts/gen-tui-oracle.mjs (drives real ../pi/packages/tui/src/utils.ts, no Pi-internal imports so no alias hook needed) + crates/pirust-tui/tests/utils_golden.rs; wired into init.sh's --check gate. Oracle coverage: CJK wide chars, emoji (single/ZWJ-family/skin-tone/flag-pair/VS16), combining marks, Thai/Lao AM vowels, tabs, ANSI SGR (single/multi/256-color/RGB/reset)+OSC-8 hyperlinks (BEL and ST terminators), mixed ANSI+tabs+wide-chars, word-wrap incl. break-long-word and CJK forced breaks, truncate with/without pad and oversized-ellipsis edge cases, strict/lenient wide-char slicing, overlay-style before/after segment extraction with style inheritance. Documented (not silent) approximation gaps, all in utils.rs module docs: RGI_Emoji sequence matching (heuristic over known emoji blocks+combinators, no Rust crate has the full Unicode table), Default_Ignorable_Code_Point (folded into Control+Format+Mark categories), cjkBreakRegex's Script_Extensions (block-range approximation). Added deps: unicode-segmentation, unicode-width, unicode-properties (workspace + pirust-tui). fmt+clippy -D warnings clean, cargo test -p pirust-tui green (8 suites), full workspace 515+ tests green, ./init.sh green with zero oracle drift. WAVE 2 DONE: crates/pirust-tui/src/{keys,stdin_buffer}.rs (1307/450 lines vs 1401/434 TS) — matches_key/parse_key/decode_kitty_printable/decode_printable_key/is_key_release/is_key_repeat/set_kitty_protocol_active/is_kitty_protocol_active + StdinBuffer's escape-sequence completeness detection (CSI/OSC/DCS/APC/SS3/old-mouse/SGR-mouse), bracketed-paste state machine, WezTerm double-escape split, Kitty-CSI-u-duplicate suppression. 306/23 oracle cases green via scripts/gen-tui-oracle.mjs's new keys/stdin-buffer sections (driving real ../pi/packages/tui/src/{keys,stdin-buffer}.ts) + tests/{keys,stdin_buffer}_golden.rs; wired into init.sh's existing --check gate. Scope decisions (documented in keys.rs module docs): KeyId/Key builder not ported (TS-compile-time-only autocomplete sugar, zero runtime behavior — matches_key/parse_key take/return plain &str/String); Kitty protocol state as a static AtomicBool (safe under #![forbid(unsafe_code)]); _lastEventType/parseEventType/KeyEventType confirmed dead state via repo-wide grep of ../pi (zero readers outside its own write site) and not ported, though the :<event> suffix is still shape-parsed so malformed sequences are still rejected; StdinBuffer::process returns Vec<StdinEvent> instead of firing EventEmitter callbacks, and the TS's setTimeout-driven flush() is redesigned as caller-scheduled (flush() itself has TS-identical semantics; Wave 4's tui.rs owns the timer). One TS-side redundancy found and documented rather than duplicated: isCompleteCsiSequence's manual mouse-SGR fallback is behaviorally identical to the regex check preceding it, implemented once. No other Rust/TS divergence found; all 329 new oracle cases matched on first run. fmt+clippy -D warnings clean, full ./init.sh green. WAVE 3 DONE: crates/pirust-tui/src/{kill_ring,undo_stack,word_navigation,keybindings,fuzzy}.rs. kill_ring.rs/undo_stack.rs (134/91 lines vs 46/28 TS) unit-tested only, per triviality (same proportionality precedent as feat-005's auth_guidance.rs). word_navigation.rs (300 vs 117 TS), keybindings.rs (472 vs 244 TS), fuzzy.rs (260 vs 137 TS) oracle-verified: 29/8/19 cases green via scripts/gen-tui-oracle.mjs's new sections (driving real ../pi TS source) + tests/{word_navigation,keybindings,fuzzy}_golden.rs; wired into init.sh. features.name: P6 — interactive pirust + built-in Rust extensions
features.description: Wire pirust-tui into pirust-coding-agent interactive mode. pirust-extension-api crate (Extension trait mirroring Pi's host surface: ~30 lifecycle events + tool/command/shortcut/flag/provider registration). ExtensionRunner trait with the BUILT-IN (compile-time) loader covering bundled extensions incl. plan-mode. Extensions are Rust, not emulated TS.

features.name: P7 — remaining ai providers + catalog generator
features.description: Remaining 10 api adapters + ~35 providers (OpenAI-completions + compat flags, Google, Bedrock SigV4, Codex WebSocket, etc.), OAuth flows, and the model-catalog generator ported into xtask (reproduces providers/data/*.json + models catalog).

features.name: P8 — pirust-orchestrator daemon
features.description: Supervisor over `pirust --mode rpc` workers via tokio::process + piped stdio; two-layer JSONL protocol over cross-platform local socket (interprocess crate); Radius remote presence with backoff. Preserve no-auto-restart asymmetry. Requires feat-012 — the workers it supervises are `--mode rpc` processes.

features.name: RPC mode (JSON-RPC over stdio)
features.description: Port modes/rpc/ (~1726 LOC: rpc-mode.ts 795, rpc-client.ts, jsonl.ts, rpc-types.ts) — the `--mode rpc` run mode that lets pirust be embedded as a subprocess, with extension UI requests proxied back over RPC. Split out of feat-005 (user decision) because its only consumer is the feat-009 orchestrator; nothing in feat-006/007 needs it. Also carries `rpc-entry.ts` (prepends `--mode rpc` to argv) and the `@file args are not supported in RPC mode` guard.

features.name: P9 — dynamic WASM extensions
features.description: Runtime-loaded user extensions compiled Rust->WASM (wasmtime/extism) behind the ExtensionRunner trait. Sandboxed alternative to Pi's in-process jiti TS loading. Authors write Rust->WASM instead of .ts; host API identical.
